text:
Jin: heads-up, canary for quantized-v3 model bump is showing +32% p99 and ~20% throughput drop on chat routes, started ~2h ago :eyes:
Ava: saw that, reproduced locally on a small batch. p50 barely moved, p99 and cpu spin up. attaching flamegraph: https://internal/fg/2480012345
Ravi: CI perf job also failed on perf/latency: https://ci/teams/infra/1234/jobs/6789 — failing threshold at p99. This is blocking rollout.
Sam: infra-bot just posted deploy event: infra-bot: "deploy/canary quantized-v3 to us-west-2" at 2480012200
Jin: timeline: we merged model-onboard PR#4872 (quantized v3 + tokenizer normalize) yesterday, then canary started this morning. suspect either kernel selection path or KV cache hit-rate change.
Ava: profiler snapshot shows a sudden increase in "generic_attention_kernel" usage vs optimized_attention_kernel when sequence length > 32. kernel selector log: `selected_kernel=generic_attention_kernel reason=kv_cache_miss_rate>0.7`
Ravi: interesting. kv_cache miss rate went from ~15% to ~78% on canary. that would force more compute and different kernel heuristics.
Sam: why would kv cache miss spike after a model bump? same model arch, different tokenizer config maybe?
Ava: I diffed tokenization outputs for the same prompt. PR#4872 added unicode NFKC normalization and changed BOS handling. many prompts now add a leading invisible char, so prefixes don't match cached prefixes. example:
```
old: "Hello, how are you?" -> tokens [502, 1024, ...]
new: "\u2060Hello, how are you?" -> tokens [12, 502, 1024, ...]
```
KV cache key is prefix-hash of token stream, so these shifts invalidate cache.
Jin: that explains bulk of misses. more misses -> larger decoded context -> different kernel path selected -> throttle/batching behavior changes and allocator churn.
Ravi: did kernel selector recently change threshold values? I checked runtime flags, nothing changed in this canary besides model and tokenizer.
ops-oncall: note: we also saw allocator warnings in staging yesterday (high vmem fragmentation) but dismissed as noise. might be related.
Sam: good catch. short-term: two options — revert PR#4872 or add a runtime compatibility shim that strips the invisible BOS if present for cache-keying.
Ava: I can prototype a shim: when computing prefix-hash, normalize with the old tokenizer's pre-tokenization mapping if model metadata contains `compat_tokenizer_version`. quick hack: `if model.meta.compat_v1: strip_unicode_marker()`
Jin: we should pause the canary rollout immediately. I've asked infra-bot to stop further rollouts.
infra-bot: "deploy/canary paused by Jin — rollback/manual action required" :white_flag:
Ravi: I'll start a git bisect on the onboard commit range to confirm it's PR#4872, but Ava's token diffs are pretty convincing.
Ravi: bisect result: culprit = onboard/commit 9f2b3e (PR#4872).
Sam: decision: revert PR#4872 from canary and add compatibility shim as a hotfix in runtime to avoid full revert in prod. create follow-ups:
- ACTION-1: Revert onboard PR#4872 in canary (Sam)
- ACTION-2: Implement prefix-compat shim and land quick patch to runtime (Ava)
- ACTION-3: Add CI perf test that checks kv_cache hit-rate before/after tokenization changes (Ravi)
Jin: also file an eval to measure distribution shift on token prefix frequency between tokenizer versions — avoid future surprises.
Ava: landing note for hotfix: will add a unit test with example prompts that showed the invisible marker, and a runtime guard that prefers model.meta.compat_v1 when present.
Ravi: after revert, monitor canary metrics for 1 hour, if p99 back to baseline we can proceed with a safer onboard plan.
Sam: creating rollout ticket: https://go/rollouts/2480012345 — tagging eng-runtime, onboard, and release.
Jin: thanks all. quick postmortem after this is stable.
Ava: small profiler snippet for the thread, for posterity:
```
flamegraph: generic_attention_kernel   38%
            optimized_attention_kernel  12%
            kv_cache_lookup             9%
            allocator_spin               14%
```
Ravi: note for follow-up: kernel selector should log `reason=token_prefix_entropy` next to `kv_cache_miss_rate` for easier triage. filing infra issue.
ops-oncall: marking incident P2, will keep monitoring alerts. :thumbsup:
Jin: locking this thread while we act. updates will be appended.
